name: Flying Jatt
summary: A Sikh martial arts teacher who gains flight and strength in Remo D'Souza's 2016 Hindi film A Flying Jatt, played by Tiger Shroff. His powers are tied to a sacred tree.
origin: Aman Dhillon is a martial arts teacher in a Punjabi neighbourhood. In the film, a lightning strike while he touches a sacred banyan tree gives him superhuman abilities, and he becomes the Flying Jatt. Remo D'Souza wrote the story and directed, with Tiger Shroff in the lead.

storyline.title: Lightning and the banyan
storyline.beat: Aman, a gentle martial arts teacher, gets his powers after being struck while touching the community's sacred tree, which bears a khanda.

storyline.title: Afraid of heights
storyline.beat: He fears heights, so he flies low at first, while his mother and brother Rohit push him to accept the hero's role.

storyline.title: A pollution-fed enemy
storyline.beat: Raka, a mercenary hired by a builder, gets pollution-fuelled powers and grows stronger in smog.

storyline.title: Accepting the dastaar
storyline.beat: Aman, who once refused a turban after being mocked for it, eventually takes it up and uses his kada in the final fight.

gossip.text: Raka is played by Nathan Jones, an Australian wrestler, as both Strange Horizons and Wikipedia note.
The Kathmandu Post found it odd that a quote credited to the director, about Mother Earth having no alternative, fills the screen near the end.
The film opened on 25 August 2016, the Janmashtami weekend.
Reviews split sharply: Hindustan Times gave 1.5 stars and DNA gave 2, while the Times of India gave 3.5 out of 5.
A tie-in graphic novel and a mobile game continued the franchise beyond the film.

quiz.q: What gives Aman Dhillon his powers in A Flying Jatt?
options: A lightning strike at a sacred banyan tree
quiz.why: He is struck by lightning while touching the community's banyan tree.
Remo D'Souza, a choreographer-turned-director, wrote and directed it.
He is afraid of heights, so he flies low.

quiz.q: What does Raka's power grow stronger in?
quiz.why: Raka's strength grows in polluted air.

theme.tagline: Saffron and sky-blue, with a banyan at his back.

timeline.title: Theatrical release
timeline.note: A Flying Jatt opens in India on 25 August over Janmashtami weekend.

timeline.title: Mixed reviews
timeline.note: Critics praise the visual effects and music but fault the script and tone; it earns about Rs 56 crore.

timeline.title: A six-song soundtrack
timeline.note: Zee Music releases the Sachin-Jigar album, including Daler Mehndi's Raj Karega Khalsa.

timeline.title: Mobile game tie-in
timeline.note: Hungama Gameshastra's mobile game based on the film is released as a tie-in during the film's release, per Wikipedia.

facts.text: Because he fears heights, Aman cruises at about the height of a car, greeting drivers and reminding them to wear seatbelts and skip their phones.
The village's wish-granting banyan has a Sikh khanda carved in it, and the same khanda is branded on Aman's back after the strike.
The final showdown moves into space, where Raka loses the pollution that feeds him, and Aman wins using his kada, the Sikh steel bracelet.
Villain Raka is hit by lightning and dumped in factory waste, gaining powers that grow in smog.
Aman's mother tells him his late father, Sardar Kartar Singh Dhillon, trained at Shaolin and was known as the Flying Jatt, so Aman inherits the name.
After his powers show up, his mother makes him a costume and screens superhero films for inspiration, then declares him a superhero at once.
She also sends him to buy vegetables on the way home from patrol, reasoning that the costume may win him a discount on the lauki.
Strange Horizons says the film stages a big rescue as a slow-motion dance to a song, after which Aman flies off so low that he has to excuse himself through news crews.
When Aman is badly hurt, his brother Rohit puts on the Flying Jatt costume to protect people, and Rohit's sacrifice sends Aman into the final fight wearing a dastaar.

Aman refuses the turban after schoolmates teased him with a midnight joke about sardars, and his mother answers by retelling a popular story of Sikhs raiding Nader Shah's camps at midnight to free captives.
A graphic novel by Thought Bubbles Studio Planet continues the story from where the film ends, and Hungama Gameshastra made a mobile game.
Aman is such a stickler for the rules that he waits for traffic lights to change even while he is flying, according to the Kathmandu Post.
Stray dogs chase Aman through the streets, and he politely begs them to chase a passing car instead.
Strange Horizons says his mother literally shoves him out of a window, telling him to go and be useful.
While picking a costume, Aman tries references from the Fantastic Four, the Hulk and Superman, and even fights tennis balls with nunchaku in Bruce Lee style.
Raka speaks about half his lines in Hindi, and Strange Horizons praises how hard Nathan Jones works to sound as if he knows the language.
Jacqueline Fernandez plays Kirti, the environment science teacher Aman loves, and Amrita Singh plays his mother, Mrs Dhillon.
Strange Horizons likens the pollution-versus-hero set-up to an Indian live-action version of the 1990s cartoon Captain Planet.
Headlines in May 2015, cited on Wikipedia, stressed that Tiger Shroff would play the Flying Jatt, not the Flying Sikh as the character had first been called.
Aman avoids the dastaar at first because, in Sikh tradition, wearing it marks the head of the household and he is not ready for that responsibility.

kidSummary: Flying Jatt is Aman Dhillon, a gentle martial arts teacher who gets powers from a lightning strike at a sacred tree. He is scared of heights, so he flies low, and with his mum's help he stops a villain who grows stronger in smog.
